items.q: What is the influence vs concern exercise?
items.a: Draw a line on paper: left = everything occupying waking hours (**concern**); right = what you can actually control (**influence**) — honestly, only **yourself**: self-talk, time management, and responses. Huberman runs it **weekly**; Andy uses it at 3 a.m. ceiling-staring or monthly for pressing worries.

items.q: How unequal are the two columns in practice?
items.a: If concern is the size of a **table**, influence is a **pin drop** on that table. Being scared about the left column "doesn't impact outcome. Everything on the **right-hand side** of the paper does."

items.q: What can you actually control when life feels chaotic?
items.a: "I have **no control** over what happens to me in my life, but I have **absolute and complete and total control** over how I respond to it." Discipline, self-control, and agency all reduce to how you spend waking hours on the **influence** side.

items.q: What does listing your concerns reveal?
items.a: An **attachment audit**: which worries are healthy vs unhealthy. Fear about uncontrollables doesn't change outcomes — actionable energy lives only in how you respond.

items.q: How has social media changed the concern column?
items.a: Feeds **inflate concern** — past classmates, old colleagues, global news — without adding influence. Reunions used to be optional; feeds make everyone from your past **permanently visible** unless you sever attention.

items.q: What laptop hack cut Andy's screen time?
items.a: Andy and Chad Wright raced to under **one hour/day**; Andy hit **~30 minutes** by moving Instagram to a laptop — "Instagram on your laptop sucks… you end up closing your laptop up." Clunky UX breaks **thumb-scroll loops**.

items.q: Do even SEALs stick with screen-time limits?
items.a: No — both selection-forged operators **reverted by March** (~60 days) despite competing. "That's all you need to know about the **platforms**" — design beats willpower alone.

items.q: Why is social media a "low-resolution" addiction?
items.a: Unlike alcohol or opioids that collapse awareness, social media keeps you **partially aware** you're wasting time while still scrolling — dual-track monitoring + scrolling. Ask: "Is the **platform working for me**, or am I working for it?"
